posts.title: Finding Steady Ground in an Unhurried Room
posts.excerpt: Beginning therapy does not require you to arrive with your thoughts neatly organized or your troubles already understood.
posts.content:
Many people spend months or even years hesitating before they arrange a first conversation with a therapist. The hesitation rarely stems from a lack of distress. More often, it arises from a quiet belief that one must first assemble an articulate explanation of what is wrong. We imagine that entering a consulting room requires a coherent narrative, clear goals, or an emotional poise that we simply do not possess in the midst of turmoil. We worry that our sadness is too vague, our anxiety too mundane, or our exhaustion too shameful to speak aloud.

At Nodoka Counselling, founded by clinical psychologist Mira Halden in 2014, our rooms at 18 Alder Row in the Riverside District were designed specifically to dissolve that expectation. When you step inside our second-floor space, there are no clipboards thrust into your hands, no clinical assessments administered against a stopwatch, and no pressure to begin at the beginning. The room holds two comfortable armchairs, a low oak table with a glass of water, and the gentle quiet of afternoon window light. The atmosphere is unhurried because human experience does not organize itself into neat chapters on command.

Your first fifty-minute conversation is not an interrogation or an evaluation. It is an initial opportunity to sit down with a dedicated professional—whether with Mira Halden, Tomas Reyes, Anika Voss, Lin Qiao, or Samuel Okafor—and see how it feels to speak honestly without having to manage the reactions of a friend, partner, or colleague. You are welcome to begin anywhere. Some people start with the persistent dread that shadows their Sunday evenings. Others speak of a recent bereavement, a relationship that has grown tense and distant, or an inexplicable weariness that sleep no longer cures.

A skilled therapist does not rush to dispense advice or impose easy solutions. Instead, they offer a steady, thoughtful presence that helps you slow down and notice what is actually happening beneath the noise of daily obligations. In an unhurried room, silence is not an awkward void to be hastily filled; it is a necessary pause where feelings can surface without being dismissed or judged. When you are given enough time and privacy, thoughts that felt tangled and frightening often begin to find their natural shape.

Taking this first step carries no obligation to commit to a long course of treatment. The process begins simply with a complimentary twenty-minute check-in call with our intake coordinator, Hana Lindqvist, followed by a single fifty-minute first conversation priced at €70. Afterwards, you are entirely free to reflect on how the meeting felt before making any further decisions. Therapy is a collaborative undertaking that belongs to you. Knowing you can pause, question, or step back at any moment is what makes genuine exploration possible.

If you are currently carrying a persistent burden of worry, grief, or exhaustion, remember that you do not need to wait until things become unbearable. You do not need to arrive with solutions, and you do not need to speak with polished clarity. Simply allowing yourself fifty minutes in a quiet room, seated across from someone who listens with careful attention, can be the quiet beginning of a different relationship with yourself and the life you are living.
